description: A single-panel figure consisting only of a rendered text table; there are no micrographs, curves or images of any specimen. The table is titled by its caption as "The chemical composition of the three different LDS alloys used for the present study". It has a two-level header: the left stub column is "Alloy designation" and the spanning super-header over the five data columns is "Elements in weight %", with the sub-headers Mn, Al, C, Ni and Fe. Horizontal rules run under the super-header and under the element row. Three alloy rows are tabulated, each entry given as value ± uncertainty (the ± tolerance is printed on a second line beneath each value). Row 1, "28Mn0Ni": Mn 28.3 ± 0.4, Al 9.0 ± 0.05, C 0.9 ± 0.01, Ni "–" (dash, i.e. not added / not measured), Fe = Balance. Row 2, "28Mn5Ni": Mn 28.1 ± 0.4, Al 8.6 ± 0.04, C 0.9 ± 0.01, Ni 4.8 ± 0.04, Fe = Balance. Row 3, "15Mn5Ni": Mn 14.7 ± 0.3, Al 9.8 ± 0.05, C 0.9 ± 0.01, Ni 4.1 ± 0.05, Fe = Balance. No error bars, plots or images accompany the table. The table documents the three Fe-Mn-Al-C-(Ni) austenitic low-density alloys whose processing and properties this study compares, and it establishes the intended Mn/Ni variation: two 28 wt.% Mn alloys differing only in Ni (0 vs ~4.8 wt.%) and one low-Mn, Ni-bearing alloy (15 wt.% Mn, 4.1 wt.% Ni) with a slightly higher Al level.

subfigures.description: Composition table with header 'Alloy designation' and super-header 'Elements in weight %' over columns Mn, Al, C, Ni, Fe. Three rows: 28Mn0Ni (28.3±0.4 Mn, 9.0±0.05 Al, 0.9±0.01 C, Ni '-', Fe Balance), 28Mn5Ni (28.1±0.4 Mn, 8.6±0.04 Al, 0.9±0.01 C, 4.8±0.04 Ni, Fe Balance) and 15Mn5Ni (14.7±0.3 Mn, 9.8±0.05 Al, 0.9±0.01 C, 4.1±0.05 Ni, Fe Balance).

observations.observation: The figure is a single composition table with the super-header 'Elements in weight %' and the column labels Mn, Al, C, Ni, Fe; the stub column label is 'Alloy designation'.
28Mn0Ni contains 28.3 ± 0.4 wt.% Mn, 9.0 ± 0.05 wt.% Al and 0.9 ± 0.01 wt.% C, with Ni marked '-', and Fe given as Balance.
28Mn5Ni contains 28.1 ± 0.4 wt.% Mn, 8.6 ± 0.04 wt.% Al, 0.9 ± 0.01 wt.% C and 4.8 ± 0.04 wt.% Ni, with Fe given as Balance.
15Mn5Ni contains 14.7 ± 0.3 wt.% Mn, 9.8 ± 0.05 wt.% Al, 0.9 ± 0.01 wt.% C and 4.1 ± 0.05 wt.% Ni, with Fe given as Balance.
The carbon content is identical at 0.9 ± 0.01 wt.% in all three alloys, so C is not a varying parameter across the alloy set.
Every tabulated value is reported with a ± uncertainty printed on a second line below the value; Fe is the balance element and carries no uncertainty.
The alloy set isolates two variables: Mn level (28 vs 15 wt.%) and Ni level (0, 4.8 and 4.1 wt.%), with 28Mn0Ni and 28Mn5Ni differing essentially only in Ni content.
The caption states this table gives the chemical composition of the three different LDS (low-density steel) alloys used for the present study.
The caption designates the alloys as LDS alloys, consistent with the Al (8.6-9.8 wt.%) and high-Mn additions tabulated that are typical of Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steels.
